description: The intermediate being is seen by beings of its own kind and by the pure divine eye; it moves with the swiftness of karmic power, has complete faculties, is unobstructed, cannot be turned back from its destination, and feeds on smells.
Driven by a perverted mind of desire the intermediate being goes to the place of its birth, attracted to the parents' union; a hell-being goes head down.
In gradual death the mind ceases at the feet, the navel or the heart, according as the dying one goes to lower destinies, to the human state, or to the gods (arhats at the heart).
At death (except for gods and hell-beings) the vital points are 'cut' by one of the elements, water and the others.
'Heat' is the first sign that the fire of the noble path, which burns the defilements, is near.
Superknowledges born of the fourth dhyāna: magical power (movement swift as mind, creation), divine ear, others' minds, former lives, death and rebirth, destruction of outflows.
A stopping of all mind and mental factors, entered from the peak of existence and emerged from with a pure mind; the life faculty and heat remain.
In the first two dhyānas bodily ease comes from tranquillity; in the third the pleasure is mental; the fourth is unmoved, free of the eight disturbances.
Even the fleshly eye of the perfect Buddhas is supramundane and its qualities cannot be fathomed in an aeon; they possess five eyes.
The Teacher and most witnesses are gone; the teaching is at its last breath and the stains are strong — a warning against heedlessness.

The first of Mahādeva's five points: an arhat may have an impure emission through the temptation of others (deities) — affirmed by the Mahāsāṃghika side per Sarvāstivāda accounts, denied by the Theravāda (Kv 2.1) and the Sarvāstivāda.
